samples.summary: `Doc.ensureHeader()`/`ensureFooter()` write without a snapshot, so the new `willWrite()` makes double-clicking the header/footer margin silently destroy the whole redo stack while creating no undo entry
samples.evidence: `Doc.ensureHeader()` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:167-175) and `ensureFooter()` (:180-188) call `store.setHeader(...)` / `store.setFooter(...)` with no preceding `snapshot()`. The only caller is `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1967 and :1972 (double-click into a margin), which also does not call `saveSnapshot()`. Before this delta redo was cleared only by `snapshot()`, so this region-creating write left redo intact; now `MemDocStore.setHeader()` calls `willWrite()` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:163) and every redo entry the user still had is thrown away by a navigation gesture — and because no checkpoint was pushed, the header creation itself is still not undoable, so the user gains nothing in exchange. On `YorkieDocStore` the same write is a `doc.update`, which both clears redo *and* pushes an undo entry, so the two stores now disagree about this path in a new way. Fix belongs at the call site (snapshot before `ensureHeader`/`ensureFooter`, or route it through `withUndoUnit`), not on the new `willWrite()`.

samples.summary: `MemSlidesStore.batch()` — which `DocStore.batch()`'s contract and `MemDocStore`'s own comment both claim to mirror — does not satisfy the batch contract this delta tightened
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:65 states the contract as "A batch that writes nothing pushes nothing" and store.ts:83 says "Mirrors `SlidesStore.batch()`"; packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:241 says "Mirrors `MemSlidesStore.batch()`". After this delta the docs store satisfies that contract by value-comparing and by moving the redo clear to `willWrite()`, while `MemSlidesStore.batch()` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789-1799) still unconditionally does `this.undoStack.push(clone(this.doc)); this.redoStack = [];` on entry and never pops — so an empty slides batch costs a dead Cmd+Z and wipes redo, exactly the two behaviours the docs store now avoids. Nothing breaks at runtime, but the shared-contract wording in store.ts and the two 'mirrors' comments now describe an implementation that no longer matches; the next person keeping the pair in step will be misled.

finding.summary: An empty batch now pops a checkpoint it did not push (the adopted `snapshot()` one), stranding writes that follow it in the same action
finding.evidence: `batch()` may now adopt the top-of-stack checkpoint (`memory.ts:222-226`) but the `wroteNothing` branch still `this.undoStack.pop()`s unconditionally (`memory.ts:251-254`). Out-of-diff callers rely on `saveSnapshot()` → `deleteSelection()` (which opens its own unit) → *more writes outside any unit*: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2500-2508` (handleBackspace), `:2551-2560` (handleDelete), `:2600-2607` (handleWordBackspace), `:2621-2630` (handleWordDelete), `:3425-3431` (handleLineBackspace). `deleteSelectionImpl` can return **false without writing** after its batch is open — `text-editor.ts:3942` (`getNormalizedRange` returns null when a selection endpoint's block is not in the layout, see `selection.ts:118`/`150`) and `text-editor.ts:3948` (`tableCellRange` whose block has no `tableData`). In that case the adopted checkpoint the preceding `saveSnapshot()` pushed is popped, the handler falls through and deletes a character with **no checkpoint on the stack**, so on `MemDocStore` (slides text boxes / table cells, the docs demo, the visual harness) that keystroke is either not undoable at all or the next Cmd+Z reverts the previous action too. Before this delta `batch()` pushed and popped its *own* clone, so the snapshot's checkpoint survived. Fix belongs on the new code: only pop when `!adopted`.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim — that the `wroteNothing` branch in `MemDocStore.batch()` pops the undo checkpoint unconditionally even when it was adopted from a preceding `snapshot()` — is not true of the code in this working tree. packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:298 reads `if (!adopted) this.undoStack.pop();`, i.e. the pop is already gated on exactly the condition the finding asks for ("Fix belongs on the new code: only pop when !adopted"). The adoption logic the finding cites is present at :256-266 (`adopted` computed by value comparison against the stack top, and `if (!adopted) this.undoStack.push(before)`), and the comment at :291-297 names the precise scenario the finding describes (TextEditor's `saveSnapshot()` then `deleteSelection()` then trailing writes) as the reason the guard exists. A repo-wide grep for `undoStack.pop()` shows the only other pop in this class is inside `undo()` at :175, guarded by `canUndo()` at :173 and unrelated to batching. Since the store never discards an adopted checkpoint, the claimed downstream harm at the text-editor call sites (writes after a `deleteSelectionImpl` early return becoming non-undoable) cannot arise from this code path, so I did not need to resolve those sites' reachability.
